meta.spec_reference: ISO/IEC 14496-12:2015 (ISO Base Media File Format), principally clause 4 (box structure), 8.2 (movie and movie header), 8.3 (track and track header), 8.4 (media, media header and handler), 8.6 (edit list and time-to-sample), 8.7 (sample tables, chunk offsets and sample auxiliary information), 8.8 (movie fragments, trex, tfhd and trun), 8.12 (protection scheme information, frma and schm), 8.16 (segment index) and clause 12 (video and sound media headers); ISO/IEC 14496-14 (MP4 file format) for the mp41/mp42 brands; ISO/IEC 23001-7 (Common Encryption) for the tenc, senc, saiz, saio and pssh boxes; the Apple QuickTime File Format specification for the qtlang language codes and the qtgfxmode graphics transfer modes, whose documentation URLs the template cites at lines 37 and 151; the MP4 Registration Authority brand registry.

schema_extensions.name: comparison_sites
schema_extensions.why: This template contains NO ReadUByte, ReadUShort, ReadByte or ReadBytes call at all, so the `lookahead` key never applies. The equivalent good-known-value set is the two switch statements: the forty-three-arm parse switch at line 469 and the display-only switch at line 203, which between them name forty-six box types. comparison_sites records both call sites with their line numbers so a value-mining pass gets the per-site sets rather than one merged list, and so the three types that appear only in the display switch - dref, free and mdat - are traceable to their source.

schema_extensions.name: bitfield_layout
schema_extensions.where: the tkhd_flags and vmhd_flags bitfield entries
schema_extensions.why: BigEndian() at line 20 makes 010 Editor pack the first-declared bitfield member into the most significant bits, but the template never states this with a BitfieldLeftToRight() call. Nothing in the base schema records bit position, yet a generator that packs the other way would put track_enabled in bit 7 instead of bit 0 - every field individually legal and the flags word completely wrong. This key names the exact bit each flag occupies within the 24-bit FullBox flags word.

schema_extensions.name: bit_width
schema_extensions.where: the fixed_value entries for tkhd_flags.dummy2, vmhd_flags.dummy2 and vmhd_flags.no_lean_ahead
schema_extensions.why: required_value_hex is specified to match the field width, but a 1-bit, 4-bit or 7-bit field has no natural hex width. bit_width states the real width so the value is not misread as a full byte.

schema_extensions.name: fixed_result
schema_extensions.where: the mp4box.default_KID, mp4box.systemID, mp4box.KID.entry, mp4box.entry.per_sample_IV, mp4box.data, mp4box.matrix_structure and mp4box.opcolor entries
schema_extensions.why: Each of these is typed calculated_value because it is a length or a derived region, yet each has a byte count the specification fixes rather than a field: 16 for a UUID, 8 for the hard-coded IV, 20 for the enca opaque block, 36 for the matrix and 6 for the opcolor. fixed_result records the constant so the rewrite step can emit it directly, while algorithm/covers/includes_self still document what it measures.

schema_extensions.name: byte_layout
schema_extensions.why: The 12-byte stride of a sidx reference and of an elst edit record is nowhere stated in the .bt - it is implicit in a struct definition elsewhere - and the rewrite step needs it to convert between an element count and the enclosing box size.

schema_extensions.name: unused_in_parse_flow
schema_extensions.why: str_stsd is typedef'd at lines 440-449 but never instantiated - the line that would have used it is commented out at line 666 and replaced by a recursive mp4box array at line 667. The flag tells the rewrite step that these entries describe declared-but-dead code, so it may wire the struct up or skip it, but must not assume it is currently reachable.

schema_extensions.name: template_deviations
schema_extensions.why: This template contains no Assert, Warning or Exit of any kind, and it disagrees with the specifications in fourteen concrete places: an unhandled box size 0 that hangs the parser rather than mis-parsing, an unguarded content-size subtraction that underflows to 2^64, version-1 movie/track/media headers read at version-0 widths, a hard-coded senc IV length, a flag tested by equality rather than by bit, a wholly wrong enca layout, a dead struct, two names for one flags field, three unsigned declarations of signed fields, and eighteen array bounds with no check. A generator that imitated the parser's laxity would emit files this template accepts and no player does, so these must be visible as data rather than buried in prose.

schema_extensions.name: cross_box emphasis in generation_range rationales
schema_extensions.where: mp4box.chunk_offset, mp4box.data_offset, mp4box.base_data_offset, mp4box.offset, mp4box.trackID and mp4box.next_track_id
schema_extensions.why: These fields are not merely bounded numbers - they are the file's only cross-references, and each must be back-patched from a measured layout or resolved against a table generated elsewhere. The schema has no key for 'this must be computed after the fact', so the requirement is stated inside each rationale where a generator author will read it alongside the bound. The chunk offset table is the single most common reason a hand-built MP4 fails to play.

meta.structure_note: A recursively nested tree of self-describing boxes with NO terminator: each box is a 32-bit size, a four-character type and optionally a 64-bit largesize, followed by either child boxes or typed fields, beginning with a mandatory 'ftyp' box at offset 0 and holding the presentation metadata in 'moov' and the sample bytes in 'mdat', with the file ending when the last box's declared size reaches the end of the file.

fp16.value.description: An 8.8 signed fixed-point number: the stored integer divided by 256 gives the real value, so 0x0100 is 1.0.

generation_range.rationale: Every use of this type in the format is a volume or a balance whose meaningful range is 0.0 to 1.0, i.e. 0 to 0x0100. Values outside that are legal 16-bit integers but describe volumes above full scale or negative balances beyond hard left, which players clamp.

fp16.value.notes: The read function at lines 175-180 divides by 0x100 to display it. Used for mvhd preferred_volume (line 758), tkhd volume (line 786) and smhd balance (line 772). ISO/IEC 14496-12 calls this the 16.16 type's 8.8 sibling and gives 0x0100 as the default full volume.

fp32.value.description: A 16.16 signed fixed-point number: the stored integer divided by 65536 gives the real value, so 0x00010000 is 1.0.

generation_range.rationale: Uses of this type are a playback rate, a track width or height in pixels, and the a/b/c/d/x/y members of the transformation matrix. Width and height are the ones that matter: 0x28000000 is 10240.0 pixels, comfortably above any real video dimension, while the full int32 range describes tracks 32768 pixels wide that a decoder will try to allocate for.

fp32.value.notes: The read function at lines 182-187 divides by 0x10000. Used for mvhd preferred_rate (line 757), tkhd width and height (lines 789-790), elst_entry media_rate (line 406) and six of the nine matrix members. 0x00010000, meaning 1.0, is the specification's default for the rate and for the matrix diagonal.

fp32uvw.value.description: A 2.30 signed fixed-point number used only for the u, v and w members of the transformation matrix: the stored integer divided by 2^30 gives the real value, so 0x40000000 is 1.0.

generation_range.rationale: The u, v and w members are the projective row of the transformation matrix and in every real file are 0, 0 and 1.0. A non-zero u or v applies a perspective warp that most decoders ignore and some reject; 0x40000000 for w is the identity value.

fp32uvw.value.notes: The read function at lines 189-194 divides by 0x40000000. ISO/IEC 14496-12 section 6.2.2: 'the point (p,q) is transformed into (p', q') using the matrix ... {u,v,w} are restricted to 0,0,1 (hex 0,0,0x40000000)'. This is the one place in the format where two different fixed-point scalings sit inside the same nine-element structure.

matrix.a.description: Horizontal scale factor of the transformation matrix; 1.0 in the unity matrix.
matrix.a.notes: ISO/IEC 14496-12 section 6.2.2 gives the unity matrix as { 0x00010000, 0, 0, 0, 0x00010000, 0, 0, 0, 0x40000000 } and says 'the matrix ... provides a transformation of video images for presentation'. In the template's member order that is a=0x00010000, b=0, u=0, c=0, d=0x00010000, v=0, x=0, y=0, w=0x40000000 - note that the fp32 members scale by 65536 while the three fp32uvw members scale by 2^30, so the diagonal is not all the same stored value. This member may legally differ from the unity value to scale, shear or translate the presentation, but the unity value is what every ordinary file carries and the only one that needs no renderer support.

fourcc.value.description: A four-character code: four bytes of printable ASCII naming a box type, a brand or a handler, never NUL-terminated and never padded with anything but spaces.
fourcc.value.pattern: ^[\x20-\x7E]{4}$ - exactly four printable ASCII characters, space-padded when the name is shorter. ISO/IEC 14496-12 additionally reserves any code whose first byte is 0xA9 (the copyright sign in Mac OS Roman) for QuickTime user-data atoms, and codes containing bytes outside 0x20-0x7E appear only in corrupt files
fourcc.value.notes: The generic four-character-code type used by boxheader.type, compatible_brand.brand, ftyp's major_brand, and hdlr's type and subtype. Its read function is at lines 248-251. The specific value sets for each of those uses are recorded on the fields themselves; this entry carries only the character-class rule that applies to all of them.

boxheader.size.description: Byte count of the whole box including this size field and the type; the values 0 and 1 are escapes rather than sizes.
boxheader.size.algorithm: byte count of the entire box - the 4-byte size, the 4-byte type, the optional 8-byte size64, and all box content. The value 1 means the real size is in the 64-bit size64 field that follows the type; the value 0 means the box extends to the end of the file and may only appear on the last box
boxheader.size.covers: the whole box from this size field to the last byte of its content, including any child boxes; it excludes everything outside the box

generation_range.rationale: The floor of 8 is a box with a size and a type and no content; anything smaller makes ContentSize() at line 167 return a negative number, which is then used as an unsigned loop bound. The 32-bit ceiling is 4 GB and the template turns this value straight into an endOffset at line 466 that drives the container walk at line 486 and the FSeek at line 495, with no check that it stays inside the file. Capping at 64 KB keeps generated files small. The escape values 0 and 1 must be emitted deliberately, never drawn.

boxheader.size.notes: ISO/IEC 14496-12 section 4.2: 'if size is 1 then the actual size is in the field largesize; if size is 0, then this box is the last one in the file, and its contents extend to the end of the file'. TEMPLATE DEVIATION: the template handles size==1 at line 374 but has NO handling for size==0 - BoxSize() at line 172 would return 0, making endOffset equal startOffset and the outer while loop at line 804 spin forever on a zero-length box. A generator must never emit size 0.

boxheader.type.description: Four-character box type; it is the sole dispatch for the entire format and the template switches on it in a forty-three-arm switch.

comparison_sites.note: the switch at line 469 dispatches on hdr.type.value; its case labels are the thirteen container types at lines 472-484 and the thirty specific types at lines 499, 502, 517, 524, 539, 557, 571, 586, 610, 620, 625, 644, 653, 662, 669, 675, 681, 687, 693, 699, 709, 715, 721, 729, 740, 750, 769, 775 and 792

a second switch in the BoxComment display function at lines 203-245 names three further types the parser has no case for - dref, free and mdat - which is where those three literals in valid_values come from

boxheader.type.notes: This template contains NO ReadUByte, ReadUShort, ReadByte or ReadBytes lookahead call, so the `lookahead` key never applies; the mineable literals are the two switch statements recorded in comparison_sites. Any type outside the switch falls to the default at line 798 and is skipped wholesale by FSkip(contentsize). ISO/IEC 14496-12 registers well over a hundred box types and the set is deliberately open - a reader must skip an unrecognised box using its size - so valid_values lists the types this template names plus the mandatory structural ones.

boxheader.size64.description: Sixty-four-bit box size, present only when the 32-bit size field holds the escape value 1; it counts the same bytes the 32-bit field would have.
boxheader.size64.algorithm: byte count of the entire box - the 4-byte size, the 4-byte type, this 8-byte field and all box content
boxheader.size64.covers: the whole box from the 32-bit size field to the last byte of its content; it excludes everything outside the box

generation_range.rationale: The floor of 16 is the 4-byte size, 4-byte type and 8-byte largesize with no content. The 64-bit ceiling is meaningless for a generated file and the value feeds the same unchecked endOffset arithmetic as the 32-bit size. The escape exists only for boxes above 4 GB - in practice only mdat - so emitting it at all is a deliberate choice.

boxheader.size64.notes: ISO/IEC 14496-12 section 4.2 calls this field `largesize`. The template's helper functions BoxSize() at line 172 and ContentSize() at line 167 both test `exists(bh.size64)` to choose between the two, and ContentSize subtracts sizeof(bh) - which is 16 when size64 is present and 8 when it is not - so the two forms are handled consistently.

compatible_brand.brand.description: A four-character brand code in the ftyp box's compatible-brands list, naming a specification the file conforms to.
value_names: ISO Base Media File Format v1
Apple QuickTime (note the two trailing spaces)
compatible_brand.brand.notes: ISO/IEC 14496-12 section 4.3: 'compatible_brands is a list, to the end of the box, of brands'. A reader accepts the file if it recognises ANY entry in this list, so including 'isom' costs four bytes and makes the file acceptable to essentially every reader. Brands are registered with the MP4 Registration Authority and the set is open; note that 'qt  ' and the iTunes brands carry significant trailing spaces.

mp4time.value.description: A timestamp in seconds since midnight on 1 January 1904, the classic Mac OS epoch, rather than the Unix epoch.

generation_range.rationale: The read function at line 270 subtracts 2082844800 to convert to the POSIX epoch, so a value below that constant renders as a date before 1970 and a value near 0 as 1904. 3082844800 is roughly the year 2001 and 4000000000 roughly 2030. The field is unsigned, but the template casts it to a signed quad at line 270 and many tools store it in a signed 32-bit type, so values above 2^31 + 2082844800 can render as negative dates.

mp4time.value.notes: The comment at lines 267-269 spells the epoch difference out. Used for create_time and modify_time in mvhd (lines 753-754), mdhd (lines 743-744) and tkhd (lines 778-779). ISO/IEC 14496-12 section 8.2.2 requires the modification time to be no earlier than the creation time, which nothing here checks.

mp4lang.value.description: Media language: either a QuickTime language code below 0x400, or three five-bit ISO 639-2 letter offsets packed into the low fifteen bits with the top bit zero.
mp4lang.value.valid_bits: bit 15 is a pad bit and must be 0; bits 14-10, 9-5 and 4-0 each hold one ISO 639-2 lowercase letter encoded as its ASCII value minus 0x60, so each of the three must be in 1-26. Values below 0x0400 are instead read as QuickTime language codes, and 32767 is the QuickTime 'unspecified' sentinel
value_names: 'und' - undetermined, the ISO 639-2 code every file may safely use
mp4lang.value.notes: Declared at line 392 and decoded by ReadLang at lines 274-287, which branches on `lang.value < 0x0400 || lang.value == qtlUnspecified` at line 276 to choose between the QuickTime enum and the packed-letter form. The qtlang enum at lines 38-149 supplies the roughly one hundred QuickTime codes, of which several are duplicate names for one value (qtlLettish and qtlLatvian are both 28, qtlSaami and qtlSami both 29, qtlGalla and qtlOromo both 87). 0x55C4 is the packed encoding of 'und', which ISO/IEC 14496-12 names as the value for unspecified language.

elst_entry.duration.description: Duration of this edit segment expressed in the movie time scale declared by the mvhd box, not the media time scale.
elst_entry.duration.algorithm: duration in movie time scale units = wall-clock seconds * mvhd time_scale; the sum over all edit entries should equal the track's tkhd duration
elst_entry.duration.covers: nothing itself; it describes how long this segment of the edit list plays

generation_range.rationale: The unit is the movie time scale, so with the conventional 600 or 1000 units per second this spans ten to a thousand seconds. A 32-bit value at the same time scale describes a movie roughly eighty days long, which a player will happily build a timeline for.

evidence.snippet: uint32 duration <name="Duration", comment="Duration of this edit segment in movie time scale units (specified in mvhd box)">;

elst_entry.duration.notes: The template's own comment on the field names the unit: 'Duration of this edit segment in movie time scale units (specified in mvhd box)'. This mixing of two time scales inside one structure is the format's most common source of quiet inconsistency.

elst_entry.media_time.description: Start time of this edit segment in the MEDIA time scale declared by the mdhd box; the value -1 marks an empty edit.
elst_entry.media_time.algorithm: start offset in media time scale units; the sentinel 0xFFFFFFFF, read as -1, means this is an empty edit that inserts silence or a blank interval
elst_entry.media_time.covers: nothing itself; it locates the start of this segment within the media

generation_range.rationale: Must point inside the media, whose length is the mdhd duration. TEMPLATE DEVIATION: the field is declared uint32 but ISO/IEC 14496-12 defines it as SIGNED, precisely so that -1 can be the empty-edit sentinel; a generator drawing an unsigned value near 0xFFFFFFFF would accidentally create an empty edit.

evidence.snippet: uint32 media_time <name="Media Time", comment="Start time of this edit segment in media time scale units (specified in mdhd box)">;

elst_entry.media_time.notes: The template's comment names the unit: 'Start time of this edit segment in media time scale units (specified in mdhd box)'. Note this is the MEDIA scale while the sibling duration field is the MOVIE scale.

elst_entry.media_rate.description: Relative playback rate for this edit segment; the specification effectively restricts it to 1.0, and 0 marks a dwell.

evidence.snippet: fp32 media_rate <name="Media Rate", comment="Relative rate at which to play this edit segment">;

elst_entry.media_rate.notes: ISO/IEC 14496-12 section 8.6.6: 'If this field is 0, then the edit is specifying a "dwell": the media at media_time is presented for the segment_duration. Otherwise this field shall contain the value 1.' So the only two legal values are 0x00010000 (rate 1.0) and 0 (dwell), and the template's fp32 type means the stored integer is 65536 times the rate.

tkhd_flags.dummy.description: The upper two of the three FullBox flag bytes of the track header; all their bits are reserved and must be zero.
tkhd_flags.dummy.notes: ISO/IEC 14496-12 section 8.3.1 defines only four track-header flag bits - track_enabled 0x1, track_in_movie 0x2, track_in_preview 0x4 and track_size_is_aspect_ratio 0x8 - all of which live in the lowest flag byte. The template's name `dummy` marks these two bytes as carrying nothing, which makes them reserved bytes that must be written as zero.

tkhd_flags.dummy2.description: The upper four bits of the low track-header flag byte; the specification assigns them no meaning, so they must be zero.
tkhd_flags.dummy2.bitfield_layout: bits 7-4 of the third flag byte - the first-declared bitfield takes the most significant bits because BigEndian() is in force at line 20
tkhd_flags.dummy2.notes: Only bits 3-0 of this byte are assigned by ISO/IEC 14496-12; the template names the remainder `dummy2` and never checks it.

tkhd_flags.track_in_poster.description: Flag bit marking the track for use in the movie's poster image; in ISO BMFF this bit position is instead track_size_is_aspect_ratio.
tkhd_flags.track_in_poster.bitfield_layout: bit 3 of the third flag byte, i.e. mask 0x08 of the 24-bit flags word
tkhd_flags.track_in_poster.notes: Read by ReadTkhdFlags at lines 305-325. ISO/IEC 14496-12 section 8.3.1: 'track_enabled: Indicates that the track is enabled. A disabled track ... is treated as if it were not present.' A track with all four bits clear is present in the file but invisible to a player, which is why track_enabled is the one whose corruption risk is high.

tkhd_flags.track_in_preview.description: Flag bit marking the track for use in the movie's preview.
tkhd_flags.track_in_preview.bitfield_layout: bit 2 of the third flag byte, i.e. mask 0x04 of the 24-bit flags word
tkhd_flags.track_in_preview.notes: Read by ReadTkhdFlags at lines 305-325. ISO/IEC 14496-12 section 8.3.1: 'track_enabled: Indicates that the track is enabled. A disabled track ... is treated as if it were not present.' then.note: a protected track must supply either a non-zero per-sample IV size or, when that is 0, a constant IV - otherwise there is no initialization vector for the decryptor at all

dependencies.description: Marking samples as protected obliges the box to supply an initialization vector one way or the other.

then.valid_bits: bits 7-4 crypt block count, bits 3-0 skip block count

structure.subject: mp4box with boxheader.type 'ftyp'
structure.detail: the File Type Box must be the first box in the file, so the four bytes 'ftyp' sit at offset 4 immediately after its size field
structure.description: ISO/IEC 14496-12 requires the ftyp box to come before any variable-length box so a reader can identify the file from its first bytes.
structure.generation_bound: exactly one, never repeated
structure.generation_note: emit as a fixed head box: a size, the literal 'ftyp', a major brand, a minor version and one to eight compatible brands - and set the size to 16 plus four times the brand count

structure.subject: mp4box with boxheader.type 'moov'
structure.detail: exactly one Movie Box is mandatory; it holds every track's metadata and without it there is no presentation
structure.description: ISO/IEC 14496-12 section 8.2.1: the MovieBox is a container for all the metadata and exactly one shall be present in a non-fragmented file.
structure.generation_bound: exactly 1 per file
structure.generation_note: emit one moov containing an mvhd and at least one trak; it may come before or after the mdat but before is what streaming requires

structure.subject: mp4box with boxheader.type 'mdat'
structure.detail: at least one Media Data Box holding the actual samples; a presentation whose chunk offsets point nowhere has no media
structure.description: The moov box's chunk offset tables are absolute file offsets that must land on real sample data.
structure.generation_bound: 1 to 2 mdat boxes, payload capped at 64 KB each
structure.generation_note: emit the mdat after the moov, then back-patch every stco or co64 chunk offset from its measured position

structure.subject: mp4box with boxheader.type 'ftyp' before every other box
structure.detail: no box may precede the ftyp; the template's own header records the file signature at line 10 as 'ftyp' at offset 4
structure.description: The file type box is the format's only signature, and it is found by position rather than by search.
structure.generation_bound: exactly one first box
structure.generation_note: emit ftyp first with no randomisation of its type bytes and no evil-bit substitution

structure.subject: none
structure.detail: ISO/IEC 14496-12 defines NO terminator, sentinel or trailer - the box stream simply ends when the file ends, and the top-level loop at line 804 runs `while (FTell() < FileSize())`
structure.description: Unlike a chunked format with an explicit end marker, an MP4 is bounded purely by its box sizes and the file length.
structure.generation_bound: not applicable - there is no tail element to repeat
structure.generation_note: do not emit any trailing marker; the last byte written is the last byte of the final box, and that box's size must reach exactly the end of the file

structure.subject: the top-level box loop
structure.detail: the parse is `while (FTell() < FileSize())`, an unbounded walk over boxes with no count field anywhere; each iteration reads one box and relies on its declared size to advance
structure.description: The whole file is an unbounded repetition of self-describing boxes, which a generator must bound explicitly.
structure.generation_bound: 4 to 12 top-level boxes per file, with mdat capped at 64 KB and every other box at 8 KB, holding generated files under about 128 KB. The loop has no progress guarantee: a box whose size is 0 or below 8 makes FTell() fail to advance and the loop spin forever.
structure.generation_note: replace the while loop with: a fixed ftyp head box, a moov, one or two mdat boxes and a bounded array of optional boxes - and give every box a size of at least 8

structure.subject: mp4box.box inside a container
structure.detail: the child walk is `while (FTell() < endOffset)`, bounded only by the parent's declared size; there is no child count field in any container box
structure.description: Container boxes hold an unbounded sequence of children delimited purely by the parent's size.
structure.generation_bound: 0 to 8 children per container, and a nesting depth of at most 6 - ftyp/moov/trak/mdia/minf/stbl/stsd is the deepest chain a normal file has. The container recursion at line 488 and the stsd entry array at line 667 are two separate recursion sites that compound, so depth must be capped explicitly or a generated box tree grows without bound.
structure.generation_note: generate children first as a bounded array, sum their sizes, then write the parent header with the measured total

structure.subject: boxheader then box content
structure.detail: every box is a 4-byte size, a 4-byte type, an optional 8-byte largesize, and then exactly the remaining declared bytes of content, with nothing between sibling boxes
structure.description: The size field is the only delimiter in the format; there are no markers at a box boundary beyond the type itself.
structure.generation_bound: one envelope per box, at most 12 top-level and 8 per container
structure.generation_note: generate each box's content first, measure it, then write the header with the measured size - the size can never be chosen before the content exists

structure.subject: mp4box with boxheader.type 'mvhd'
structure.detail: the Movie Box must contain exactly one Movie Header Box, and it must come before the track boxes
structure.description: ISO/IEC 14496-12 section 8.2.2: the MovieHeaderBox defines the presentation-wide time scale and duration every track's values are relative to.
structure.generation_bound: exactly 1 per moov
structure.generation_note: emit mvhd as the first child of moov, then the trak boxes

structure.subject: mp4box with boxheader.type 'trak'
structure.detail: the Movie Box must contain at least one Track Box, and each must contain a tkhd and an mdia
structure.description: A presentation with no tracks has no media to play.
structure.generation_bound: 1 to 2 traks per file
structure.generation_note: emit each trak as tkhd followed by mdia; the tkhd track_id must be unique and non-zero

structure.subject: trak, mdia, minf, stbl nesting
structure.detail: a track's metadata is a fixed chain of containers: trak holds tkhd and mdia, mdia holds mdhd, hdlr and minf, minf holds a media header, dinf and stbl, and stbl holds the sample tables
structure.description: ISO/IEC 14496-12 fixes this nesting; a demuxer walks it by name and a missing level makes the track undecodable.
structure.generation_bound: one such chain per track, at most 2 tracks
structure.generation_note: generate the chain innermost-first - the sample tables, then stbl, then minf, then mdia, then trak - so each container's size is written from a measured total

structure.subject: mp4box with boxheader.type 'stsd'
structure.detail: the Sample Table Box must contain a Sample Description Box; without it the samples have no codec configuration
structure.description: Every sample references a sample description by one-based index, so at least one entry must exist.
structure.generation_bound: exactly 1 stsd per stbl, with exactly 1 entry
structure.generation_note: emit stsd with entry_count 1 and a single sample entry box whose type is the codec's four-character code

structure.subject: mp4box with boxheader.type 'stsz'
structure.detail: requires stts, stsc and either stco or co64 in the same stbl, and all four must agree about the sample and chunk counts
structure.description: The four sample tables are one index split across four boxes: sizes, timing, chunk mapping and chunk locations.
structure.generation_bound: one of each per stbl, entry counts capped at 256
structure.generation_note: generate the four tables together from one list of samples, then write each box's count from the measured list

structure.subject: stco and co64
structure.detail: a Sample Table Box carries either the 32-bit Chunk Offset Box or the 64-bit Chunk Large Offset Box, never both
structure.description: The two boxes hold the same table at different widths; co64 exists only for files above 4 GB.
structure.generation_bound: exactly one of the two per stbl
structure.generation_note: emit stco unless the file genuinely exceeds 4 GB, which a bounded generated file never will

structure.subject: mp4box with boxheader.type 'moof' after 'moov'
structure.detail: every Movie Fragment Box must follow the Movie Box, and fragments must appear in increasing mfhd sequence_number order
structure.description: A fragment carries only the deltas from the defaults the moov's mvex box establishes, so the moov must be read first.
structure.generation_bound: 0 to 4 fragments per file
structure.generation_note: if generating a fragmented file, emit moov with an mvex, then the moof/mdat pairs with sequence numbers 1, 2, 3 ...

structure.subject: mp4box with boxheader.type 'moof'
structure.detail: requires an mvex box inside the moov declaring the per-track defaults, and each traf inside the moof requires a tfhd naming a track that exists
structure.description: ISO/IEC 14496-12 section 8.8.1: the MovieExtendsBox warns a reader that the file is fragmented and supplies the trex defaults.
structure.generation_bound: one mvex per file, one tfhd per traf
structure.generation_note: emit mvex with one trex per track before any fragment, and give each traf a tfhd whose trackID matches a real tkhd

structure.subject: moof then its mdat
structure.detail: each Movie Fragment Box is immediately followed by the media data its trun boxes reference, because trun data offsets are measured from the moof
structure.description: The fragment's sample data is located relative to the moof itself, so separating the two invalidates every offset.
structure.generation_bound: one mdat per moof, capped at 64 KB
structure.generation_note: emit the pair as one indivisible element and back-patch the trun data_offset from the measured distance

structure.subject: boxheader.size equal to 0
structure.detail: the extends-to-end-of-file escape must never be emitted: BoxSize() returns 0, endOffset equals startOffset, and both the container walk and the top-level loop spin without progress
structure.description: A legal specification escape that this template cannot parse at all, making it a hang rather than a mis-parse.
structure.generation_bound: not applicable - this is an exclusion
structure.generation_note: always emit a real size of at least 8, and for the last box make it reach exactly the end of the file

structure.subject: boxheader.size below 8
structure.detail: a size of 2 to 7 is smaller than the header it is part of, so ContentSize() underflows to a huge unsigned value that the default arm then FSkips
structure.description: The content-size computation is an unguarded subtraction, so an undersized box is an enormous skip rather than a small one.
structure.generation_bound: not applicable - this is an exclusion
structure.generation_note: give every box a size of at least 8, or at least 16 when the 64-bit largesize form is used

structure.subject: endianness
structure.detail: BigEndian() is set at line 20 and never changed, so every size, offset, count and fixed-point value in the file is network byte order
structure.description: MP4 inherits QuickTime's big-endian convention throughout; there is no byte-order mark and no little-endian variant.
structure.generation_bound: not applicable - this is a global encoding rule
structure.generation_note: write every multi-byte field big-endian, and note that the four-character codes are char arrays written in reading order rather than byte-swapped integers

structure.subject: mp4box.brand inside ftyp
structure.detail: the compatible-brands list runs to the end of the ftyp box with no count field, so its length is (box content size - 8) / 4
structure.description: This is the one repeating element in the format whose count comes purely from the enclosing box size.
structure.generation_bound: 1 to 8 brands, i.e. 4 to 32 bytes
structure.generation_note: choose the brand list first, then set the ftyp size to 16 plus four times its length so the loop consumes exactly whole brands

structure.subject: mp4box with boxheader.type 'hdlr'
structure.detail: each Media Box must contain a Handler Reference Box whose subtype declares the track kind
structure.description: The handler subtype is what tells a demuxer whether to expect a vmhd or an smhd inside minf, and which sample entry format to expect in stsd.
structure.generation_bound: exactly 1 per mdia
structure.generation_note: emit hdlr with a zero pre_defined type and a subtype of 'vide' or 'soun', matching the media header that follows

template_deviations.subject: box size 0 is unhandled and hangs the parser
template_deviations.issue: ISO/IEC 14496-12 section 4.2 defines size 0 as 'this box is the last one in the file, and its contents extend to the end of the file'. The template handles size==1 at line 374 but has no case for 0: BoxSize() at line 172 returns 0, so endOffset equals startOffset, the container walk at line 486 makes no progress and the top-level loop at line 804 never advances.
template_deviations.impact: A legal file whose last box uses the extends-to-EOF escape makes this template loop forever. It is a hang, not a mis-parse.
template_deviations.action: Never emit size 0; give the last box a real size that reaches exactly the end of the file.

template_deviations.subject: ContentSize underflows for undersized boxes
template_deviations.issue: ContentSize() at line 167 computes `size - sizeof(bh)` with no check that the size is at least the header size, and the result is returned as an unsigned 64-bit value.
template_deviations.impact: A box size of 2 to 7 - or a largesize of 0 to 15 - produces a content size near 2^64, which the default arm's FSkip at line 799 then applies, seeking far past the end of the file.
template_deviations.action: Give every box a size of at least 8, or 16 with the largesize form.

template_deviations.subject: version-1 mvhd, tkhd and mdhd are mis-parsed
template_deviations.issue: ISO/IEC 14496-12 makes the creation time, modification time and duration 64-bit when the FullBox version is 1, but the mvhd arm at lines 751-767, the tkhd arm at lines 776-790 and the mdhd arm at lines 741-748 all read the version byte and then read only the version-0 32-bit widths.
template_deviations.impact: Every field from the creation time onward is read at the wrong offset in a version-1 header, which is the form long or recent presentations use.
template_deviations.action: Emit version 0 in mvhd, tkhd and mdhd.

template_deviations.subject: the senc per-sample IV length is hard-coded to 8
template_deviations.issue: ISO/IEC 23001-7 makes each senc entry's IV exactly default_per_sample_IV_size bytes, which the tenc box may set to 8 or 16. The template declares `byte per_sample_IV[8]` unconditionally.
template_deviations.impact: A 16-byte-IV file has every senc entry read 8 bytes short, shifting every byte after the first entry.
template_deviations.action: Pair a default_per_sample_IV_size of 8 with this hard-coded length, or avoid senc entirely.

template_deviations.subject: the senc subsample flag is tested by equality rather than by bit
template_deviations.issue: The guard reads `if(flag[2] == 2)` rather than `if((flag[2] & 2) != 0)`, unlike every other flag test in the template.
template_deviations.impact: A senc box whose flags are 3 - subsample data present together with another bit - is parsed as though it had no subsample table, shifting every entry.
template_deviations.action: Emit flag[2] as exactly 2 when subsample data is present and exactly 0 otherwise.

template_deviations.subject: the enca sample entry is read with the wrong shape
template_deviations.issue: An AudioSampleEntry is six reserved bytes, a data reference index, eight reserved bytes, a channel count, a sample size, pre-defined, reserved and a 16.16 sample rate, followed by child boxes. The enca arm at lines 669-674 reads a version byte, three flag bytes and an entry_count that the box does not have, then twenty opaque bytes.
template_deviations.impact: The box is mis-parsed from its first byte and its child boxes are never reached.
template_deviations.action: Avoid enca; use a plain stsd entry whose type the switch does not name, so the default arm skips it cleanly.

template_deviations.subject: str_stsd is declared but never instantiated
template_deviations.issue: The struct is typedef'd at lines 440-449 with its own commented-out box loop at lines 444-448, and the line that would have used it is commented out at line 666 in favour of a recursive `mp4box entries[entry_count]` at line 667.
template_deviations.impact: Two constraints entries describe declared-but-dead code. The replacement is actually more correct - a sample entry IS a box - but it makes stsd a second recursion site alongside the container walk.
template_deviations.action: Cap the stsd entry_count at 1 and cap the overall box nesting depth.

template_deviations.subject: two names for one flags field, and two spellings of one parameter
template_deviations.issue: The FullBox flag bytes are called `flag` in twenty switch arms and `flags` in five (lines 717, 731, 742, 752, 771). The saio arm spells its aux parameter `aud_info_type_parameter` at line 563 while the saiz arm spells the identical field `aux_info_type_parameter` at line 577.
template_deviations.impact: Four distinct constraints keys describe two format fields, which a rewrite step must not treat as four independent values.
template_deviations.action: Treat mp4box.flag and mp4box.flags as one field, and the two parameter spellings as one.

template_deviations.subject: several fields are declared unsigned where the specification makes them signed
template_deviations.issue: elst_entry.media_time at line 405 is uint32 where ISO/IEC 14496-12 makes it signed so -1 can mark an empty edit; mp4box.data_offset at line 591 is uint32 where the specification makes it signed so data may precede the moof; mp4box.layer at line 784 is uint16 where the specification makes it signed.
template_deviations.impact: Each sentinel or negative value reads as a huge positive number, and a generator drawing unsigned values near the top of the range creates empty edits and backward offsets by accident.
template_deviations.action: Treat all three as signed and keep generated values well inside the positive range.

template_deviations.subject: frma codingName and schm scheme_type are declared uint32 rather than fourcc
template_deviations.issue: Both fields carry four ASCII bytes - 'avc1', 'cenc' and so on - but are declared as 32-bit integers at lines 500 and 520, so 010 displays them as numbers.
template_deviations.impact: Nothing for parsing, but a value-mining pass over the template sees no string literals for these two fields even though their legal sets are four-character codes.
template_deviations.action: Emit the big-endian numeric equivalents of the four-character codes.

template_deviations.subject: no size or count field is ever bounds-checked
template_deviations.issue: entry_count, sample_count, KID_count, DataSize, reference_count, num_entries and default_constant_IV_size are all used directly as array bounds with no check against the enclosing box's content size or the file size, at lines 510, 514, 534, 537, 555, 567, 569, 583, 593, 642, 667, 679, 685, 691, 697, 706, 713 and 719.
template_deviations.impact: A 32-bit count with an 8- or 12-byte element size claims tens of gigabytes from four header bytes; the stsd case additionally multiplies with the box recursion.
template_deviations.action: Cap every count as recorded in the generation ranges and derive each from the entries actually written.

template_deviations.subject: no Assert, Warning or Exit anywhere in the file
template_deviations.issue: The template contains no validation guard of any kind. Its only diagnostic is the Printf at lines 491-494, which notes when a child box's declared size does not match the bytes it consumed and then FSeeks past the discrepancy at line 495 anyway. No magic number, no brand, no version and no length is ever checked.
template_deviations.impact: The set of files this template accepts is very much larger than the set of valid MP4s, so its behaviour is no guide to validity.
template_deviations.action: Take every 'spec'-sourced constraint in this file as binding despite the template's silence.

template_deviations.subject: no ReadUByte, ReadUShort, ReadByte or ReadBytes call anywhere
template_deviations.issue: The template performs no lookahead of any kind. Every branch is taken on a field already read, and the dispatch is the switch on hdr.type.value at line 469 plus the display-only switch at line 203.
template_deviations.impact: The `lookahead` schema key never applies. The mineable literals are the two switch statements, whose case labels give the forty-six box types recorded in boxheader.type.
template_deviations.action: Treat the two switch statements as the good-known-value set in place of lookahead call sites.

template_deviations.subject: the qtlang enum contains duplicate values
template_deviations.issue: qtlLettish and qtlLatvian are both 28 (lines 68-69), qtlSaami and qtlSami both 29 (lines 70-71), and qtlGalla and qtlOromo both 87 (lines 128-129). The enum also has no explicit base type, unlike qtgfxmode.
template_deviations.impact: A value-mining pass over the enum sees 100 names but only 97 distinct values, and EnumToString picks whichever name 010 resolves first.
template_deviations.action: Treat the mp4lang value as the packed ISO 639-2 form rather than a QuickTime code; 0x55C4, meaning 'und', is safe under both readings.
